chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I asked him about wiping over the khuffayn and the turban, so he said: "The Book has preceded the khuffayn," and he said: "Do not wipe over a khuff."

key_terms.اَلْخُفَّيْنِ: the two leather socks worn on the feet
key_terms.اَلْكِتَابُ: the Qur'an as the governing revealed text
key_terms.اَلْمَسْحِ: wiping in the context of ritual purification
key_terms.خُفٍّ: a leather sock over which wiping is being forbidden

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about wiping over khuffayn in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution), rejecting wiping over leather socks. It grounds the ruling in the precedence of the Book, indicating that the Qur'anic prescription governs this issue.
